function.description: Retrieves the current weather conditions for a specified city and state. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which to get the weather, in the format of 'City, State', such as 'San Francisco, CA' if State for the city exists. 'City, Country' if State for the city doesn't exist.

**Java – A quick primer** | Topic | What you’ll find | |-------|------------------| | **What is it?** | Java is a high‑level, class‑based, object‑oriented programming language designed with the philosophy “write once, run anywhere” (WORA). It was created by James Gosling at Sun Microsystems (now owned by Oracle) and released publicly in 1995. | | **Core idea** | Code compiled into bytecode runs on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM), allowing the same program to execute on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android devices, embedded systems, servers, and more without modification. | | **Key characteristics** | • Strongly typed
• Automatic memory management (garbage collection)
• Rich standard library (java.lang.*, java.util.* …)
• Threaded concurrency support
• Security sandbox (especially important for applets & web apps)
• Platform independence via JVM | | **Typical use cases** | • Web application backends (Spring Boot, Jakarta EE)
• Enterprise software (ERP, CRM, banking platforms)
• Mobile apps (Android SDK)
• Desktop GUIs (Swing, JavaFX)
• Big‑data processing (Apache Hadoop, Spark)
• Embedded/IoT devices (Arduino, Raspberry Pi libraries)
• Game development (LibGDX, jMonkeyEngine) | | **Evolution timeline** | *1991–95*: Development → JDK 1.0 release.
*2002*: Java 2 Platform, Standard Edition (J2SE) becomes Java SE 5.0 (introduces generics, annotations, enhanced enums).
*2018*: Java 9 introduces modules (JPMS).
*2020s*: Regular six‑month releases (e.g., Java 21 in September 2023) bring new APIs, performance improvements, and long‑term support (LTS) versions like Java 11, Java 17, Java 23… | | **Syntax basics** | ```java\npublic class HelloWorld {\n public static void main(String[] args) {\n System.out.println(\"Hello, world!\");\n }\n}\n``` | | **Compilation vs execution** | `javac MyClass.java` ➜ compiles to `MyClass.class`.
`java MyClass` ➜ loads `.class`, interprets bytecode via JVM. | | **Popular frameworks/libraries** | Spring/Spring Boot, Hibernate/JPA, Apache Commons, Jackson, Logback, Mockito, JUnit, Vert.x, Micronaut, Quarkus. | | **Learning resources** | • Official docs: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/
• Online courses: Coursera’s “Java Programming”, Udemy’s “Java Mastery”, Pluralsight, freeCodeCamp YouTube tutorials.
• Books: “Effective Java” (Joshua Bloch), “Head First Java”. | ### Quick FAQ | Question | Answer | |----------|--------| | **Why still popular after all these years?** | Mature ecosystem, huge community, robust tooling (IntelliJ IDEA, Eclipse, NetBeans), strong corporate backing, extensive libraries, cross‑platform nature. | | **How does Java compare to Kotlin or Scala?** | Kotlin offers concise syntax, null safety, coroutines—great for Android and modern backend work. Scala adds functional paradigms but has steeper learning curve. Java remains the lingua franca because of its stability and widespread adoption. | | **Can I write mobile apps directly in Java?** | Yes, Android supports Java natively (though many projects now favor Kotlin). For iOS, you'd typically use Swift/Objective‑C, not Java. | | **Do I need a license?** | No. Since Java 7, Oracle provides open source builds under GPLv2+CE. Many distributions (OpenJDK, Amazon Corretto, AdoptOpenJDK) offer free binaries. | | **Where do I start coding?** | Install JDK (≥ 17 LTS recommended), set up your IDE, create a simple “Hello World,” then explore classes, objects, inheritance, interfaces, collections, streams, lambdas, and finally build a small project using Maven/Gradle. | --- #### TL;DR *Java is a versatile, platform‑independent programming language built around the JVM, used across enterprise, cloud, mobile, desktop, and embedded domains. Its rich ecosystem, mature tooling, and consistent evolution keep it relevant even decades after its debut.*
